Man zahlet zum voraus <PRIZE>45. xr.</PRIZE> und bey Empfang des gantzen Werckes annoch <PRIZE>45. xr.</PRIZE> das weitere kan aus dem Project verstanden werden.</ITEM>",
  "number_of_fixes": 1,
  "explanation": "The XML was not well-formed. Inside <BIBL> there was one opening <TITLE> tag but two closing </TITLE> tags. The first title, 'Geschrey um Mitternacht, siehe der Bräutigam kommt: Gehet hinaus ihme entgegen.', was correctly opened and closed. The alternative title introduced by 'Oder,' ('38. Predigten von dem jüngsten Gericht ... uc.') ended with a </TITLE> that had no matching opening tag. This follows the usual early-modern practice of giving a main title and a subtitle joined by 'Oder'. So the fix was to add an opening <TITLE> tag directly after 'Oder, '. The connective word itself stays outside both titles. The nested <VOLUME> elements (38. and 4.) now sit inside the second <TITLE>, and all tags are correctly nested within <BIBL> and <ITEM>. No other structural errors were found. Some observations were deliberately left unchanged so the text and tag set stay intact. First, the character sequences such as \u221a\u00fc (√ü), \u221a\u00a7 (√§) and \u221a\u00ba (√∫) are encoding errors (mojibake) for ß, ä and ü. They do not affect well-formedness. Second, 'Septembris' is a month rather than a year, so the <YEAR> tag is semantically questionable. Third, <PRIZE> presumably means 'price' (45 Kreuzer, abbreviated 'xr.'). Fourth, 'siehel' and 'Andang' are likely OCR errors for 'siehe' and 'Anhang'."
